test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 English Previous Paper 1 (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Have you / ever spoke / to anyone / about your problems?
solution: The correct answer is** '​****ever spoke'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. • Here,** 'ever spoken' **should be used instead of **'ever spoke'.** • The structure of these kinds of sentences is as follows: • **HAVE + Subject ( I, You, We, You, They ) + V3 (third form of main verb – past participle). ** • *​Example: **Have** you **started** taking lectures?* • Hence, '**spoken**' should be used instead of '**spoke**'. **Correct Sentence:__** *Have you **ever spoken** to anyone about your problems?* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। • यहाँ** 'even spoke'** के स्थान पर **'ever spoken' **का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए। • इस प्रकार के वाक्यों की संरचना इस प्रकार है: • HAVE + Subject ( I, You, We, You, They ) + V3 (third form of main verb – past participle). • *​Example: **Have you started **taking lectures?* • अतः '**spoke**' के स्थान पर '**spoken**' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए। eb:Tc6c, The correct answer is '**DACB**'.
